subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Arch: Rome's Structural Secret
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Arch: Rome's Structural Secret usable.

hook.text: A flat stone beam breaks under its own weight after a few meters. An arch can span 30.

buildup.text: Arches convert downward force into outward thrust. Each stone pushes on its neighbor, not the ground.

discovery.text: The keystone at the top locks everything in place. Remove it, and the entire arch collapses.

twist.text: Romans didn't invent the arch. Mesopotamians did, 4,000 years earlier. Rome just scaled it up.

climax.text: Aqueducts, bridges, the Colosseum — nearly every Roman marvel depends on the arch.

punchline.text: Gravity is the enemy. The arch makes it an ally.

quiz.question: What role does the keystone play in an arch?
options: It absorbs most of the weight so other stones bear less load
It locks all the other stones in place under compression
It is purely decorative and can be removed safely
